answer: Agents trading jetty surveys, haven maps, and trellis designs allocate dispute votes in proportion to tokens locked in escrow, with a 30-day withdrawal delay. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives the same total voting weight as one agent holding 100 tokens. To control a majority, an attacker must lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for at least 30 days regardless of how many identities it creates.
